manifest_status_reason: The environment's network policy was changed to Full access after the initial DATA_ACQUISITION_BLOCKED pass. Under Full access: cyberjapandata.gsi.go.jp, maps.gsi.go.jp, and nlftp.mlit.go.jp (MLIT KSJ) became reachable and real data was acquired from them (railway + station: MLIT KSJ N02, bracketed 2008/2011 editions; terrain: GSI DEM10B; roads: MLIT KSJ N13, 2024-only). fgd.gsi.go.jp and mapps.gsi.go.jp remained unreachable (502) even under Full access, on repeated attempts — so 基盤地図情報 (building footprints, road edges/curbs as a distinct dataset from KSJ N13, and the GSI aerial-photo viewer UI) are still not acquired. Buildings and historical aerial photo review remain blocked/unavailable; buildings are still Directive 01 SYNTHETIC placeholders. See evidence/sources.json for per-host status and evidence/reconstruction.json for how each new item's confidence was derived.

datasets.note: Genuine imagery WAS acquired and reviewed (seamlessphoto), but it could not serve as 2010 evidence: the same composite shows large ground-mounted solar panel arrays near the station, which postdate 2010 in Japan, proving this specific imagery is not contemporaneous. It was used only for a qualitative layout sanity-check and to cross-validate the direction of the MLIT KSJ railway data (matched). No year-specific 2007-2012 aerial photo tiles exist for this location at all (404, confirmed not a tile-math bug). mapps.gsi.go.jp itself (the service that would let a human browse metadata like capture date/operator) remained unreachable throughout. Net result: no building/road existence claims in this pass rely on aerial confirmation for 2010 specifically — this is a real, confirmed gap, not a silently-worked-around one.

next_steps_for_user_provided_data: Drop real files under public/data/worlds/JP_HOKKAIDO_KIYOSATO_MIDORI_20100530/reality/ (or anywhere, and point world.json at them).

GeoJSON already exported from GSI/MLIT/OSM tooling: run `node scripts/import-geojson.mjs <input.geojson> <type> <out.geojson>` to normalize into the RealityData shape (confidence/source_ids/historical_status prompted or passed as flags).
DEM as ESRI ASCII Grid (.asc): run `node scripts/convert-dem-asc.mjs <input.asc> <out dem.json>`.
DEM as GSI GML (JPGIS2.0): not yet supported — convert to .asc or GeoJSON with external GIS tooling (e.g. QGIS) first.
After adding/replacing any file, run `npm run validate` (scripts/validate-reality-data.mjs) before relying on it.
